items.summary: Anthropic PBC is pursuing what could become the largest first-time share sale ever, seeking up to US$64.4 billion in its IPO and US$26 billion privately, with a fully diluted valuation near US$1.4 trillion.
items.title: Anthropic's Oversubscribed IPO Aims for Record Scale Amid AI Spending Surge

items.summary: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigned Thursday amid reports of extramarital affairs, including one with Alice Huang, whom US authorities suspect is a Chinese spy. His departure triggered Nvidia shares to fall 14% at market open and revived bipartisan calls in Congress for tougher restrictions on advanced AI chip exports to China.
items.title: Nvidia's Jensen Huang Resignation Sparks Calls for China Chip Export Crackdown

items.summary: The Information reported on Nov. 12 that ByteDance, TikTok's Chinese owner, plans to buy back up to $6 billion of shares from existing investors at a valuation of about $400 billion, citing a letter to shareholders and one source familiar with the plan; Reuters could not immediately verify it.
items.title: ByteDance Plans $6 Billion Share Buyback at ~$400 Billion Valuation

items.summary: Nvidia co-founder and CEO Jensen Huang resigned effective immediately after reports surfaced of extramarital affairs, one involving a businesswoman US intelligence suspects was feeding information to Beijing — allegations China denies. Colette Kress, CFO since 2013, became interim CEO while the board named its first chairman, Harvey C. Jones. Nvidia said it investigated whether Huang faced a foreign intelligence effort but found no evidence of compromised secrets or national security breaches. Trump called Huang an "honorable guy" and suggested Tim Cook as successor; critics decried his involvement. Nvidia shares fell about 5 per cent Thursday.
items.title: Why Jensen Huang Resigned as Nvidia CEO

items.summary: The MSCI Asia Pacific Index rose 0.3%, led by South Korea, as US equity futures advanced on Nasdaq 100 and S&P 500 contracts. Nvidia fell 4.3% after Jensen Huang was ousted, but rivals Broadcom and AMD rallied over 5%. Oil held near $88.70 a barrel while Treasury yields climbed amid expectations of faster Fed rate hikes.
items.title: Asian Stocks Rise After Nvidia CEO Ouster; Oil Steady Amid Fed Hike Fears

items.summary: On November 12, 2026 Google launched Gemini 4 Hydrogen as the family's lowest-cost member. Its $0.10/$0.50 price is only a 25% discount versus Carbon and Argon (both doubling December 1), yet it remains roughly 15x pricier than Claude Haiku 5.5 and GPT-6 Luna at those rates. Google frames Hydrogen as the new free tier powering Search, but test output shows stark quality gaps despite near-equal pricing with its siblings.
items.title: Google's Gemini 4 Hydrogen pricing and positioning amid sibling model confusion

items.summary: Microsoft has begun restoring services after a widespread global outage disrupted access to its Microsoft 365 suite, including Outlook, Teams, Word, Excel, PowerPoint, SharePoint and OneDrive. The company said affected servers had been returned to service and remained stable so far while shifting traffic to alternative routes. Nearly 130,000 users worldwide reported problems at the peak, according to Downdetector.
items.title: Microsoft Begins Restoring Services After Global Outage Hits Microsoft 365 Suite

items.summary: A global Microsoft outage affected tens of thousands of users, with reports peaking at nearly 140,000 around 18:00 GMT Thursday. Services including Teams, Outlook and Copilot experienced connectivity problems. Microsoft said it restored part of its service but warned servers could become unresponsive again under traffic. The issue spread to AI firms OpenAI and Anthropic, which reported connector failures.
items.title: Microsoft Global Outage Disrupts Outlook and Teams

items.summary: Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick faces renewed scrutiny over his handling of Megaspeed, an AI chip firm tied to a Chinese national with whom former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang had an affair. A growing GOP contingent accuses him of defying President Trump by failing to blacklist the company or restrict AI exports to China; Rep. John Moolenaar claims Trump directed three times that Megaspeed be blacklisted. Yet most Republicans defend Lutnick, and even some staunch allies blame his conduct. The White House stands firmly behind him, praising his trade policies—citing nearly 20 fair trade deals secured under his tenure—and calling him the most transformative Commerce Secretary in modern history.
items.title: Nvidia Fallout Fuels Questions About Lutnick's Staying Power

items.summary: India's retail inflation reached a two-year high of 6.09% in October, breaching the Reserve Bank of India's 6% tolerance limit and strengthening expectations of another rate hike in December. Headline CPI rose to 6.1%, driven by broad-based price pressures across 11 of 12 major categories, with food inflation at 8.51%. Core inflation stood at 4.6%, while the RBI projects headline inflation at 5.2% for FY27 and a core rate of 4.4%. Economists from CareEdge Ratings and Barclays India anticipate measured hikes—likely a 25-basis-point increase in December, with some forecasting terminal hikes into February 2027.
items.title: India's Inflation Tops RBI Ceiling; December Rate Hike Expected

items.summary: President Trump said he spoke with Jensen Huang Wednesday but was unsure whether it had been established that Alice Huang, a Chinese businesswoman linked to intelligence services, was a spy. Fresh reports allege this is a third affair: Kimberly Powell and Alice Huang preceded her. The NYT reported the video capture in San Jose; the WSJ tied Alice Huang to Huang's apology letter.
items.title: Trump Unsure Whether Nvidia-Linked Businesswoman Was a Spy; Reports of Third Affair Emerge

items.summary: After Jensen Huang resigned amid personal misconduct allegations, Nvidia's shares plunged, raising fears about AI infrastructure. Rob Day of Spring Lane Capital models a likely middle scenario: slowed but non-collapsing build-outs that ease market froth while sparing power-supply deals and exposing neoclouds. Analyst Kunjan Sobhani warns losing Huang's relationships could hurt fundraising beyond 2028, though near-term chip commitments look safe; the Hugging Face acquisition faces DOJ review. Nvidia's $105 billion guarantees for SB Energy's OpenAI-backed PORTS-Pike campus in Ohio are risky bets that pricing debt unlocks cheaper capital.
items.title: Nvidia's CEO Shakeup and the AI-Energy Fallout

items.summary: On Nov 13, Singtel reported a 55% fall in first-half net profit to $1.54 billion from $3.4 billion a year earlier, driven by the absence of $2.21 billion in exceptional gains from its Airtel stake sale and Intouch-Gulf Energy merger. Underlying net profit rose 10% to S$1.49 billion as NCS, Digital InfraCo and Optus strengthened; operating revenue grew 6% to $7.29 billion. The board approved a $0.09 interim dividend per share, shares closed at $4.15 on Nov 12, and the group raised full-year OpCo Ebit growth guidance to mid-to-high single digits.
items.title: Singtel H1 net profit falls 55% to S$1.54 billion on lack of divestment gains; underlying profit up 10%

items.summary: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigned Thursday after admitting an affair with Alice Huang, a Megaspeed executive and alleged Chinese spy. His departure raises concerns about whether Nvidia will continue championing open-source AI under interim CFO Colette Kress, especially amid the stalled $13 billion Hugging Face acquisition.
items.title: Jensen Huang's Exit Puts Nvidia's Open-Source Support in Question

items.summary: Nvidia announced Thursday that Jensen Huang resigned immediately after 33 years leading the AI chipmaker, amid reports of board reviews over personal-conduct allegations. Trump publicly endorsed former Apple CEO Tim Cook as his ideal replacement, though no indication exists that Cook is being considered or would leave Apple. Colette Kress was named interim CEO while the board evaluates internal and external candidates.
items.title: Trump backs Tim Cook as Nvidia CEO successor

items.summary: Nvidia shares plunged more than 10%, with some reports citing over 11%, after co-founder Jensen Huang resigned as chief executive officer, triggering a broader selloff in AI-linked stocks. The chipmaker reportedly lost nearly $750 billion in market capitalisation since the controversy began, while several US neocloud companies recorded double-digit declines.
items.title: Nvidia shares crash over 10% after Jensen Huang's exit; $750 billion wiped out as AI stocks tumble

items.summary: Ethiopia's latest conflict in Tigray, a resumption of the two-year war that ended in 2022, is contested as effectively over. Federal forces quickly captured Mekelle after the TPLF withdrew, but residents report continued fighting with heavy artillery and drone strikes across central, northern and north-western regions. Analysts diverge sharply: Cameroon Hudson sees a weakened TPLF unable to sustain major conflict, while Yared Tibebu warns of a possible prolonged war as the group prepares for counteroffensives.
items.title: Is Ethiopia's Tigray Conflict Really Over?

items.summary: President Donald Trump floated a new strategy for his war against Iran, suggesting the conflict could end without a deal limiting Tehran's nuclear program. On Thursday, he said he told Vice President JD Vance not to negotiate with Iran and that such days have passed, signaling confidence the U.S. can leave the situation in limbo.
items.title: Trump Pulls Vance from Iran Talks in Bet on Shaky Status Quo

items.summary: Pat Cummins held an hour-long press conference disputing Usman Khawaja's assertion that ball tampering was known about in 2018, calling it 'complete and utter nonsense.' Cummins said Khawaja had been 'casual' with people's lives and reputations. He acknowledged seeing ball tampering during the Sheffield Shield but declined to identify who or which team was involved.
items.title: Cummins Slams Khawaja Over Ball-Tampering Claims in Hour-Long Press Conference

items.summary: Republican lawmakers in Ohio are circulating a draft bill that would prevent coal-fired plants from closing when owners have contractual obligations to shut down, applying to both past and future contracts. The proposal directly targets the 620-megawatt Cardinal unit at Buckeye Power's plant in eastern Ohio, slated to close by end of 2028 under a settlement reached with American Electric Power. Sierra Club's Neil Waggoner calls it unconstitutional as retroactive legislation, while Democratic Rep. Tristan Rader opposes it and questions whether it will pass before the Dec. 31 lame-duck session ends.
items.title: Ohio GOP Bill Would Block Coal Plant Closures Despite Settlements

items.summary: Nvidia is searching for a permanent CEO after co-founder Jensen Huang resigned amid allegations of extramarital affairs, including one involving an alleged Chinese spy. CFO Colette Kress was named interim leader and could stay permanently. Candidates include Ian Buck, Rene Haas, Lisa Su of AMD, and Harvey C Jones as new board chair. Nvidia holds a ~$4tn market cap.
items.title: Who Could Replace Jensen Huang as Nvidia CEO?

items.summary: The controversy around Nvidia co-founder Jensen Huang has intensified after reports that the former CEO had an intimate relationship with a second company employee. This follows his resignation amid allegations of two other extramarital relationships, including one with Kimberly Powell, vice president of healthcare, captured affectionately on video at a San Jose conference in March 2026.
items.title: ‘Huang-gate’ deepens as former Nvidia CEO reportedly had relationship with another employee

items.summary: Nvidia's co-founder and CEO Jensen Huang resigned on Thursday after revelations of two extramarital affairs, including one with a woman suspected of spying for China. CFO Colette Kress will serve as interim CEO while the company searches for a permanent successor, with engineer Ian Buck also cited by analysts. The scandal has drawn scrutiny toward Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick and prompted speculation about his future under President Trump, who had urged Huang to fight on but floated Tim Cook as an alternative leader.
items.title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang Resigns Amid Scandal; Trump and Officials React

items.summary: The controversy surrounding Nvidia co-founder Jensen Huang has deepened with reports that the former CEO had an intimate relationship with a second employee, Kimberly Powell, vice president of healthcare. This follows allegations involving Alice Huang, whom US intelligence officials suspect of links to Chinese services, adding a national security dimension. The revelations intensify scrutiny over his conduct and Nvidia's leadership.
items.title: Huang-Gate Deepens As Former Nvidia CEO Reportedly Linked To Second Employee

items.summary: Jensen Huang's resignation after 33 years left Nvidia with interim CEO Colette Kress and no permanent successor, triggering a 7.80% drop as AI peers like CoreWeave (-14%) and Nebius (-20%) slid. Analysts warn of potential 20% corrections, though historical comparisons to Intel and HP CEO departures remain limited given Nvidia's unique scale.
items.title: Nvidia Stock After Jensen Huang Exit: Crash or Rally?

items.summary: Jensen Huang stepped down as Nvidia CEO amid an extramarital affair with Alice Huang, a Chinese businesswoman linked to Beijing intelligence. CFO Colette Kress was named interim CEO while the board seeks a permanent successor among internal and external candidates. Board chair Harvey Jones praised Kress for guiding extraordinary growth. The company declined to state a resignation reason but launched an independent investigation into foreign-intelligence targeting.
items.title: Nvidia Names Colette Kress Interim CEO After Jensen Huang's Exit

items.summary: This article argues that Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's ouster—following revelations of affairs with a woman suspected by U.S. authorities of being a Chinese spy and running a Singapore-based neocloud—is damaging the AI industry at precisely the moment he was championing it across five fronts. As its loudest advocate for open-weight models, proponent of self-regulation over government oversight, defender of the 'AI as tool' narrative, architect of an emerging Nvidia-powered AI PC market, and driver of aggressive data-center financing schemes (including $750 billion in circular deals), Huang has lost his influence just when these initiatives most needed it. His replacement will struggle to replicate this momentum amid ongoing congressional scrutiny and reputational fallout.
items.title: Five Ways Jensen Huang's Ouster Could Damage the AI Industry

items.summary: ZDNET reports that Fitbit users are unable to view several key health metrics in the Google Health app, including breathing rate, blood oxygen, resting heart rate, HRV and skin temperature. Reddit users speculate the glitch began after updating to Fitbit 5.12. One user noted it appeared about six days ago. Google says it is aware of the issue and working on a resolution.
items.title: Fitbit Users Lose Google Health Metrics After Update

items.summary: Microsoft 365 outage service credits apply only to subscriptions sold through the Cloud Solution Provider (CSP) program, not direct purchases. Only CSP direct and indirect providers can file claims as Partner Center support tickets; indirect resellers cannot, so customers must route requests through their provider's Admin agent role. Credits are prorated by affected service and outage duration rather than fixed, with qualifying scenarios detailed in the Online Services Consolidated SLA. Azure uses a separate filing deadline from other services, and approved credits require a tenant GUID, outage ID found in the admin center, and customer email.
items.title: How Businesses Claim Microsoft 365 Outage Service Credits Under CSP

items.summary: Jensen Huang's resignation removes what columnist Liz calls the 'Nvidia put,' a backstop that has underpinned the entire AI ecosystem. Nvidia guarantees over $100 billion in data-center leases, owns $51 billion of private-company stock and another $63 billion listed. Its balance sheet absorbed market fears and propped stocks and 401(k)s for years. His replacement faces higher stakes akin to Tim Cook after Steve Jobs.
items.title: The End of the 'Nvidia Put' That Powers AI

items.summary: The sixth round of India-Canada negotiations for a Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement (CEPA) is underway, with both sides aiming to conclude by November ahead of Prime Minister Narendra Modi's December visit. Discussions center on professional mobility under the services chapter, including skilled-worker quotas and student movement. Canada hosts 1.8 million people of Indian origin. Trade data shows Canadian goods exports worth C$9.68 billion in Q1 2026 (15.56% of India's $6.51 billion pulse imports), while bilateral trade reached C$13.55 billion in goods and C$19.62 billion in services for 2025. Trade minister Maninder Sidhu targets doubling bilateral trade to $70 billion by 2030, citing energy, LNG and nuclear cooperation.
items.title: India-Canada CEPA Negotiations Focus on Professional Mobility and Trade Expansion

items.summary: Lakehouse//RT is a real-time analytics engine built on Databricks that serves queries directly from the lakehouse, avoiding separate serving layers and duplicated data. It targets AI-agent workloads generating sustained concurrency beyond traditional warehouse design, delivering sub-100 millisecond latency at 12,000 queries per second in beta. Rather than scaling cost with demand, it scales efficiency by finishing each query faster so capacity frees sooner. Customers report large gains: Aurasell consolidated clusters and cut costs 10x while sustaining over 250 QPS; VisionHeight reduced costs more than 90% from Apache Pinot; nOps cut infrastructure spending 6x after migrating from Apache Druid, eliminating duplicated data.
items.title: Databricks Lakehouse//RT Scales Real-Time Analytics Without Proportional Cost Growth

items.summary: According to the Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD) International Migration Outlook - 2026 report, Indians again led advanced economies in citizenship acquisition. Between 2020 and 2024, around 9.25 lakh Indian citizens obtained nationality of an OECD member country, while these countries granted nearly 87L new citizenships overall. In the prior five-year period, about 65 lakh individuals acquired such nationality, with Indians comprising roughly 10%.
items.title: Indians Top OECD Citizenship Acquisitions Again in Five-Year Period

items.summary: Rajasthan's Special Summary Revision (SSR) draft roll records about 5.26 crore voters, roughly 11 lakh more than the final SIR roll but still below the State Election Commission's earlier figure of 5.45 crore. The SSR method carries existing voters forward without re-verification, unlike the deeper house-to-house SIR exercise.
items.title: Rajasthan's SSR Draft Roll Shows Wide Variation From Other Official Voter Counts

items.summary: Following the November 2026 midterms, Rep. Jim Jordan (R-Ohio) was elected minority leader of the incoming House Republican conference after stepping down as chairman of the Judiciary Committee. Law professor David Kaye and advocates like Brandi Geurkink and Nina Jankowicz see hope that oversight will refocus on exposing tech-corporate influence rather than attacking disinformation researchers, regulators, and Europe's Digital Services Act—though none view this as ending the broader fight over online speech. Kenneth Haar warns Trump may still wield a tougher game with the EU. Kaye expects Raskin to pursue hearings into alleged censorship in early 2027.
items.title: Will a New Congress Ease Pressure on Europe's Digital Regulations?

items.summary: As Ireland hosts its EU Council presidency amid protests against data center expansion, critics argue its draft revisions to the Cloud and AI Development Act (CADA) favor Big Tech. Research group SOMO found Google, Microsoft, and Amazon—controlling 70% of Europe's cloud market—held 41 meetings with the Commission before CADA was announced. Ireland's amendments lower barriers for US hyperscalers to qualify as 'sovereign,' undermining Europe's stated goal of reducing dependence on American tech giants. Researchers warn that capital committed to data centers could have built roughly 50,000 homes in Ireland between 2019 and 2024. With an NBC exit poll citing 56% of voters prioritizing data centers and AI, the article questions whether Ireland should prioritize democratic oversight or industry interests.
items.title: Ireland's EU Presidency and the Data Center Sovereignty Debate

items.summary: Estate agents are increasingly using artificial intelligence to enhance property listing images, a practice dubbed "housefishing" that experts warn can mislead buyers. Olivia Nicole found her south-west London viewing did not match the enhanced Rightmove photos, which also appeared on Zoopla and Winkworth; all three companies said they had strict AI guidelines and removed the images. A survey of 906 UK homebuyers found one in five who bought a home last year viewed digitally enhanced listings. Jack Bushrod notes agents should label enhancements but draws the line at misleading changes, while Cara trusts Howards after it began labelling all AI photos. Trading Standards says basic enhancement is legal if disclosed, but structurally altering rooms or hiding features could break the law.
items.title: The rise of 'housefishing' - when does using AI go from enhancing to misleading?

items.summary: The Indian rupee weakened to 94.04, down 35 paise amid rising dollar demand driven by hotter-than-expected US inflation data and higher treasury yields, combined with roughly $900 million of importer buying. Strong state-bank bids added pressure as the pair slipped past 94.00 after trading between 93.61 and 95.06. Foreign portfolio inflows of ₹7,830.6 crore into equities partially offset the decline.
items.title: Indian Rupee Falls as Dollar Demand Weighs on Currency

items.summary: The US government expanded an AI advisory tool for air traffic controllers across the entire national airspace system, according to a November 10 agency statement. The $875 million SMART system has rerouted 180 flights since September 21 in Washington DC airspace, saving about 10 minutes and nearly 80 gallons of fuel per flight on average. Airline executives support the rollout; the controllers' union says it was not involved in designing or testing the system.
items.title: FAA Expands AI Air Traffic Tool Nationwide

items.summary: European leaders face pressure to name a single representative for upcoming Russia-Ukraine peace talks, after US envoy Steve Witkoff confirmed Europeans would attend. The Dublin European Political Community summit of 47 leaders revealed frustration at being sidelined while the US holds two seats. Figures like Kaja Kallas and Antonio Costa are tipped as likely representatives, though many national leaders prefer personal attendance. Public divisions surfaced—Italian PM Giorgia Meloni criticized disarray in a letter to Costa, while Estonian PM Kristen Michal warned Europe is trapped by Russia's security demands. Leaders also cited breached agreements, including the 1994 Budapest Memorandum. Meanwhile, funding disputes overshadow talks: the EU identified a €70 billion shortfall in promised aid for Ukraine.
items.title: EU Leaders Tussle Over Who Will Represent Europe in Ukraine Peace Talks

items.summary: Elisabeth Braw of the Atlantic Council argues Russia pursues hybrid warfare through hoax threats and cyber attacks to weaken European nations. She asserts that Russia exploits its knowledge that Europe will not retaliate with equivalent illegal or unethical measures. This asymmetry allows Moscow to increase its power at Europe's expense while avoiding reciprocal responses, according to Sharon Gaffney of FRANCE 24.
items.title: Russia's Hybrid Warfare Strategy Against Europe, Per Atlantic Council Expert

items.summary: The proposed India-Canada Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement offers potential market access for West Bengal's tea industry, which is grappling with declining production and shrinking exports. Overseas shipments fell nearly 46 percent from 3.95 million kg in 2015 to 2.13 million kg in 2025. Rising EU pesticide-residue scrutiny threatens compliance, particularly around nicotine limits reduced toward 0.4 mg/kg by February 2026 and field trial residues reaching 5 mg/kg versus India's 3 mg/kg domestic limit. Testing costs of Rs 9,000 plus GST per sample strain smaller growers who depend on bought-leaf factories.
items.title: Canada Deal Opens a Door, but Darjeeling Tea Faces a Compliance Wall

items.summary: Footage shows newly elected members of the US House ascending the Capitol steps after a mandatory orientation programme for first-time lawmakers, drawn from states including Illinois, Iowa, Michigan, New York and Virginia. Their arrival follows November's midterm elections, which brought sweeping Democratic gains and fewer Republican newcomers. Incoming politicians will study legislative operations before the 120th Congress convenes on 3 January 2027.
items.title: New US Congress Members Pose at Capitol

items.summary: Finnish officials confirmed a Russian Buyan-M corvette, Naro-Fominsk, was hit Wednesday in the Gulf of Finland during an operation targeting Russia's Ust-Luga oil export depot. Ukraine's SBU said drones flew near Estonia and briefly into Estonian airspace from Latvia; NATO aircraft were airborne but deemed it unsafe to intervene. The Baltic Sea fleet remained untouched.
items.title: Russian warship struck by Ukrainian drone in Gulf of Finland

items.summary: Senior journalist N Ram doubts that semi-retired Sonia Gandhi will intervene behind the scenes to mend the alliance between the Congress and Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam (DMK), which she revived in 2004 but has since fractured. In her memoir Belonging: A Journey of Love, Sonia recounts setting aside personal misgivings about allying with the DMK despite fears of betraying assassinated husband Rajiv Gandhi and lingering Jain Commission findings linking the party to Tamil Eelam separatists. Ram attributes today's rift not to that history but to unrealistic seat-sharing demands driven by Rahul Gandhi, who he blames for abruptly aligning Congress with TVK without consulting MK Stalin. He contrasts Sonia's pragmatic coalition-building with what he sees as the present leadership's rigidity.
items.title: Can Sonia Gandhi repair broken Congress-DMK ties?

items.summary: Retired four-star General Jack Keane, a director of REalloys (NASDAQ: ALOY), warned that China has signaled its willingness to use American dependence on rare earths as leverage against U.S. defense production. The urgency is underscored by an expiring truce keeping Beijing's October 2025 export restrictions on hold until January 10, 2027, just nine days after the Pentagon's new magnet sourcing rules take effect on January 1, 2027. China has already demonstrated its leverage: in April and October 2025 it restricted dysprosium, terbium and military-use exports, forcing Ford to shut plants for three weeks. To counter this vulnerability, the Army selected REalloys to build a plant at Utah's Tooele Army Depot under a proposed 75-year lease (initial 50 years plus 25 renewal), with first dysprosium-terbium production targeted for early 2027 from Saskatchewan and Greenland sources. The deal remains non-binding pending site plans, environmental reviews and permits.
items.title: U.S. General Warns of China's Rare Earth Leverage as Pentagon Secures Domestic Supply Chain

items.summary: The U.S. Justice Department, with stablecoin issuers Tether and Circle (entity-325-362), froze $2.7 billion of funds tied to the Oct. 29 breach of Binance, the world's largest crypto exchange, which lost $6.3 billion—the biggest theft on record—attributed by the FBI to North Korea's TraderTraitor group.
items.title: US Freezes $2.7 Billion After North Korea's Binance Hack

items.summary: sonnen and SOLRITE Energy announced integrating ADAPT Energy's controls with Eaton AbleEdge smart breakers into their virtual power plant, letting home batteries shed nonessential loads like pool pumps during grid stress or outages. The system coordinates automatically with the battery, restores circuits when power returns without rewiring, reduces installation complexity, and requires homeowner opt-in for pre-approved load shedding.
items.title: sonnen and SOLRITE Add Smart Breakers to Virtual Power Plant

items.summary: Israel's Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's office dismissed reports of a heated phone call with US President Donald Trump over Iran, calling them "fake news." While anonymous sources described the exchange as tense and one called it a "shouting match from hell," officials denied any confrontation. The dispute reflects deeper disagreements: Netanyahu pushed for renewed military strikes against Tehran, while Trump favored diplomatic negotiations.
items.title: Netanyahu Rejects 'Shouting Match' With Trump

items.summary: Footage shows newly elected members of the US House of Representatives gathering on the Capitol steps after November's midterm elections, which brought sweeping gains for Democrats and a smaller Republican intake. The freshman cohort attended mandatory orientation covering parliamentary protocol before the 120th Congress convenes on 3 January 2027.
items.title: New US Congress Members Pose for Traditional Photo at Capitol

items.summary: Britain and Azerbaijan signed a Joint Declaration on a Strategic Partnership in Ireland during the European Political Community Summit, with British Prime Minister Andy Burnham and Azerbaijani President Ilham Aliyev as signatories. The declaration reaffirms long-term commitment to strengthening defense cooperation focused on training, capacity building and interoperability, while exploring enhanced defense industry collaboration. Both nations also aim to broaden trade and investment ties, promote economic growth, support the Middle Corridor development, and deepen education cooperation through an annual Strategic Partnership meeting.
items.title: UK and Azerbaijan Sign Strategic Partnership Deal at European Political Community Summit

items.summary: At midnight in Illinois, hemp-derived THC drinks became illegal under a last-minute federal provision and the state's own law. Companies rushed to sell or ship remaining stock: Playdate discounted its NA rosé, leaving less than a truckload for Sammy Dorf and Brian Ward; Go Brewing's Joe Chura made his final Easy Man batch about a month ago; Perfectly Dosed shipped a metric ton of emulsion containing more than 100m mg THC to Wisconsin; and Crescent Canna sold pallets to buyers including former NBA players. Confusion surrounds the ban amid an association lawsuit, though any pause applies only to suing businesses. Uncertainty over enforcement looms as distributors may refuse products regardless.
items.title: Illinois Hemp-THC Drink Ban Forces Manufacturers Into Inventory Fire Sale

items.summary: This year, drone and missile strikes have caused unprecedented damage to data centers in Eastern Europe and the Middle East, disrupting cloud services for millions and permanently deleting some Amazon Web Services customer data. This poses a new concern for Big Tech, governments, and everyone relying on shared digital infrastructure. Analyst Joseph Jarnecki of RUSI will host a live conversation titled “Drone attacks and data centers: New Risks for Big Tech” on Tuesday, November 17 at 1 pm ET to explore these implications.
items.title: Drone Attacks on Data Centers Threaten Cloud Resilience for Big Tech and Society

items.summary: On a packed final day of the Web Summit in Lisbon, speakers moderated by Euronews addressed Jensen Huang's resignation as Nvidia CEO amid revelations of two extramarital affairs—one reportedly suspected of spying for China—and warnings about an AI bubble and soaring US debt. Nvidia stock fell roughly 15% at open but settled around $164 per share, down over 30% from its October high. Panelists Adam Kobeissi and James Galbraith cautioned that public-debt markets could trigger the next financial crisis, with interest consuming 19% of US revenue; Kobeissi warned of a 100% bankruptcy risk while remaining bullish on the resilient economy.
items.title: Jensen Huang's Nvidia Exit and Debt-Crisis Fears Dominate Web Summit's Final Day

items.summary: Crude prices fell roughly 20% from a late-October peak of $118 per barrel, pressured by de-escalation hopes amid stalled Ukraine-Russia talks and the U.S.-Iran standoff. Despite rebounding Hormuz flows, elevated insurance and record tanker rates keep shipping costs high, while Iranian demands for frozen-fund release and Gulf producers' diversification into Red Sea routes sustain a floor near $94.
items.title: Oil Prices Squeezed Between Peace Hopes and Iran Escalation Risk

items.summary: The World Food Program reports acute food insecurity affecting 28.8 million people across the Democratic Republic of Congo, with some 3.6 million in emergency conditions per Integrated Food Security Phase Classification data covering September to November 2026.
items.title: Hunger Crisis Deepens in DR Congo as 28.8M Face Acute Food Insecurity

items.summary: On Nov 13, Asian equities steadied after a turbulent week marked by the resignation of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang amid reports of extramarital affairs. His departure raised concerns about US chip export policy and AI supply chains. The MSCI Asia-Pacific index (ex-Japan) rose 0.26%, reversing part of its prior-day fall, while South Korea's Kospi gained 2.35% and Japan's Nikkei added 1.4%. Rising Treasury yields lifted the dollar to a weekly gain of 0.9%, weighing on the yen near 160 per dollar. Investors now price a 14.5% chance of a jumbo 50-basis-point Fed hike in December, boosting risk assets despite ongoing AI-infrastructure regulatory fears.
items.title: Asian Stocks Recover as Nvidia Turmoil and Hawkish Fed Expectations Drive Markets Higher

items.summary: A major global Microsoft outage is affecting tens of thousands of users, with reports peaking at nearly 140,000 around 18:00 GMT Thursday. Services including Outlook, Teams and AI software Copilot suffered connectivity problems as servers were unexpectedly unavailable, straining remaining systems. Messaging remained largely functional. The disruption impacted Microsoft 365 customers worldwide—including the US, Japan and Singapore—and affected other companies like Anthropic and OpenAI. No cyber-attack was indicated.
items.title: Microsoft Global Outage Disrupts Outlook, Teams and Copilot Worldwide

items.summary: A widespread outage struck Microsoft platforms on Thursday, disrupting email access for nearly 130,000 users tracked by Downdetector just after 1 p.m. ET, with many unable to send or receive messages. Issues also affected Teams, Copilot, and other Microsoft 365 services. Redmond-based Microsoft said it was investigating connectivity errors tied to Exchange Online mailboxes in the Americas, attributing them to elevated infrastructure load and servers failing automated health checks, while rolling out a fix.
items.title: Widespread Microsoft Outage Hits Outlook and Other Apps

items.summary: A widespread outage has disrupted Microsoft's Outlook email service, affecting users' ability to access inboxes and send or receive messages. The disruptions have prompted concerns among individuals and businesses dependent on the platform for daily communication. Reports also indicate related issues with Microsoft 365 and Teams, as Microsoft works to restore full access.
items.title: Microsoft Outlook Outage Disrupts Users Worldwide

items.summary: Nvidia co-founder Jensen Huang forfeited roughly $108 million in unvested restricted stock units after stepping down following revelations of two extramarital affairs. The forfeiture represents about 0.08% of his estimated $138.4 billion net worth, which derives almost entirely from Nvidia common shares comprising nearly 97% of his wealth.
items.title: Jensen Huang Forfeits $108 Million in Unvested Nvidia Equity

items.summary: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang admitted three extramarital affairs, one reportedly with Alice Huang, a former executive at Singapore-based Megaspeed International suspected of working for Beijing. The US Justice Department is investigating whether Megaspeed violated export-control laws by facilitating Chinese access to restricted AI chips. Ms Huang's role remains unestablished publicly. Nvidia's stock hit a 14-year low relative to earnings this week, and the crisis prompted his resignation after 33 years of leadership. Framing it as espionage reveals how China's Ministry of State Security cultivates contacts across business and academia, while its Network Security Police Offices—more than 1,000 in at least 10 major firms—are embedded within tech companies. The fallout risks chilling scientific, academic and commercial exchange between the two nations.
items.title: Nvidia's Jensen Huang scandal brings China's spy networks into view

items.summary: The White House is considering removing Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick amid criticism over US export controls to China, intensified by controversy surrounding Nvidia co-founder Jensen Huang's alleged ties to Alice Huang, suspected of Beijing intelligence links. Lawmakers question why advanced technology shipments were not restricted; the administration has held off blacklisting flagged companies since October 2025.
items.title: White House Weighs Ouster of Commerce Secretary Lutnick Over China Chip Controls

items.summary: Jensen Huang, who stepped down as Nvidia's CEO on November 12 amid allegations of three extramarital affairs and a relationship with businesswoman Alice Huang—whom US authorities suspect of spying for Beijing—has agreed to testify before Capitol Hill lawmakers. Negotiations are underway regarding the timing and format of his appearance.
items.title: Former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang to testify before Congress over alleged China spy link

items.summary: After CEO Jensen Huang resigned, Nvidia shares fell as much as 14% intraday but closed 4.3% lower at $166.19, erasing nearly $500 billion in a month and wiping out over $1 trillion in market capitalization below the $4 trillion level not seen since July 2025.
items.title: Nvidia's $1 Trillion Market Cap Drop After Jensen Huang Resignation

items.summary: A widespread outage struck Microsoft platforms Thursday, disrupting Outlook email for nearly 130,000 users on Downdetector just after 1 p.m., before reports declined. Users reported trouble sending or receiving mail and loading inboxes. Thousands also faced issues with Teams, Copilot, and broader Microsoft 365 services. Redmond-based Microsoft said it was investigating email and Teams disruptions, noting elevated infrastructure load likely contributed to connectivity errors as some servers failed automated health checks; a fix was being tested.
items.title: Widespread Outage Hits Microsoft Email and Other Apps

items.summary: A report claims ousted Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang was in an intimate relationship with a second employee, whose name is not known. This revelation follows two earlier extramarital affairs that led to his departure from the company on Thursday evening. The women involved are Alice Huang, suspected of being a Chinese spy, and Kimberly Powell, Nvidia's vice president of healthcare.
items.title: Nvidia's Jensen Huang had relationship with second employee amid ongoing scandal

items.summary: A widespread outage struck Microsoft platforms on Thursday, disrupting Outlook email for nearly 130,000 users reported via Downdetector shortly after 1 pm. Users faced inbox-loading failures and messaging problems across Outlook, Teams, Copilot, and broader Microsoft 365 services. Redmond-based Microsoft cited elevated infrastructure load and servers failing automated health checks as likely causes while testing fixes; Exchange Online mailboxes were restored in North America.
items.title: Widespread Microsoft Outage Hits Email and Teams

items.summary: Jensen Huang resigned amid reports of two extramarital affairs, one involving a businesswoman suspected to work for China's intelligence services. Colette Kress will serve as interim CEO while retaining her CFO role; the board considers both insiders and outsiders for the permanent position. Investors worry Nvidia may scale back data center financing under new leadership, slowing the AI boom.
items.title: Nvidia's leadership transition raises investor concerns over AI financing

items.summary: Nvidia's board appointed Colette Kress as interim CEO while initiating a permanent succession search, and named Harvey C. Jones its first chairman. Jensen Huang, who co-founded the company in 1993 and holds roughly 3.61% of shares, is departing after more than three decades at the helm. His exit raises questions about Nvidia's investments in OpenAI, Anthropic and CoreWeave amid investor scrutiny over circular AI financing. The transition coincides with an extramarital affair controversy involving Alice Huang and Megaspeed, plus a reported relationship with Kimberly Powell. Huang's hands-on management style—overseeing around 60 direct reports—and his ties to US policy add further uncertainty.
items.title: Nvidia's Leadership Transition Amid Controversy and AI Ecosystem Uncertainty

items.summary: Four AFL players investigated over an alleged sexual assault at a Melbourne hotel will not be charged, police said on insufficient evidence. The four Sydney Swans men - Isaac Heeney, James Jordon, Chad Warner and Nick Blakey - had been season-long suspended after inviting women to the Pullman Hotel following a game in August. A fifth player, Riley Bice, was already cleared. Three adult entertainers plan civil action.
items.title: AFL Players Cleared After Hotel Incident Investigation

items.summary: President Volodymyr Zelensky welcomed a US pledge by envoys Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff to include European Union delegates in the next round of peace talks with Russia. The meetings followed shuttle diplomacy between Putin, who said Russia's territorial demands are unchanged, and failed Abu Dhabi negotiations. Separately, Ukraine agreed its largest prisoner swap since 2022, while roughly one-fifth of Ukraine remains under Russian control.
items.title: Zelensky Welcomes EU Inclusion in Russia-Ukraine Peace Talks

items.summary: The US dollar rose toward a 19-month high as traders priced in a larger-than-usual Federal Reserve rate hike next month, with two-year Treasury yields gaining 34 basis points. Inflation remains stubbornly elevated, and the CME FedWatch tool showed a 14.5% chance of a large hike versus 0% last week. The yen briefly touched 160 per dollar, prompting Japanese Finance Minister Satsuki Katayama to vow action on currency volatility.
items.title: Dollar nears 19-month high on Fed hike bets; yen tests 160

items.summary: US envoy Jared Kushner said Thursday that Russia and Ukraine agreed to expand the next round of talks to include European nations, with Washington working toward what he called the war's largest prisoner exchange. The envoys met Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky in Dublin after talks with Russian counterpart Vladimir Putin in Moscow.
items.title: Kushner and Zelensky Confirm Europe Joins Next Russia-Ukraine Talks Round

items.summary: The United States has reopened direct, secretive talks with Myanmar's military-backed government—the same regime Washington accuses of genocide—marking a reversal from efforts to isolate the junta after its 2021 coup. Analysts suggest US interest in Myanmar's rare earth resources may drive diplomacy, and that Adam Castillo's detention served as 'hostage diplomacy' for direct contact. The outreach raises alarms among human rights advocates concerned about rehabilitating leadership accused of atrocities. For Min Aung Hlaing, the engagement represents a diplomatic breakthrough following his February 2021 coup against Nobel laureate Aung San Suu Kyi.
items.title: US Reopens Secretive Talks With Myanmar's Military Regime Amid Rare Earth and Sanctions Debate

items.summary: India's tyre sector is growing revenues but losing margins amid surging crude oil and rubber costs. Ceat posted 26% revenue growth to ₹4,762 crore yet saw EBITDA margins fall from 13.5% to 9.5%, with net profit down 40%. The problem spans MRF, Balkrishna Industries, Apollo Tyres and JK Tyre—JK's margin dropped to 6.9% from 12.1%. Oil-based materials make up 60-70% of tyre costs, while India imports roughly half its natural rubber needs. With raw materials at two-thirds of production costs and prices locked in OEM contracts, makers must raise replacement-market prices gradually or risk losing customers to retreading.
items.title: Rising Input Costs Erode India's Tyre Makers' Profit Margins Despite Record Sales

items.summary: A Scroll newsletter by Shoaib Daniyal examines why domestic air and rail travel have stalled in India. Air passenger growth has flattened, while fares rose sharply enough that a litigant sought Supreme Court price caps; the bench dismissed it with 'Don't travel by air.' An airline oligopoly—shrunk from over a dozen carriers to two—leaves customers unable to escape gouging. Rail data shows second-class passengers being priced out since 2013, though AC three-tier bookings grew nearly fourfold between 2012 and 2025 before declining slightly in fiscal 2026. Analysts suggest income growth has deepened rather than widened: benefits have accrued to existing middle- and upper-income groups instead of broad-based expansion, now pressuring even those classes as air traffic falls.
items.title: Why has air and rail travel stopped growing in India?

items.summary: At least eight people died when a three-storey building collapsed at the edge of a construction site on Flatbush Avenue in Brooklyn, New York City's mayor Zohran Mamdani said Thursday. At least 17 others were injured, including three firefighters, per Mayor Mamdani. Search crews worked through overnight hours amid rubble, pulling out victims and at least one survivor, including a pregnant woman hoisted to an ambulance Wednesday night; it remains unclear how many may still be trapped. The building gave way Wednesday afternoon while workers excavated the neighbouring lot. City officials said a stop-work order had been issued in March over inadequate overhead protection during demolition, with violations found again in April before work resumed in May.
items.title: Death Toll Rises to 8 in Brooklyn Building Collapse as Rescuers Search for Survivors

items.summary: Samajwadi Party president Akhilesh Yadav launched a sharp attack on Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath, accusing him of insulting Lord Krishna through remarks about cowherds (Gopalaks). Describing the alleged remarks as “unforgivable”, the SP chief questioned the CM’s commitment to Sanatan Dharma. He also referenced Ram temple donation controversies in Ayodhya and accused Varanasi authorities of disrespecting the Pal community, while urging restraint from public representatives holding constitutional duties. Confidence: 0.98
items.title: UP Politics: Akhilesh Yadav Accuses Yogi Adityanath Of Insulting Lord Krishna, Questions His Sanatan Dharma Credentials
